note: Hebrew zovo tame hu, "his discharge, it is unclean"; the KJV supplies "because of" and makes the man the subject, while the plain syntax declares the discharge itself unclean (the man's uncleanness follows in v. 3).

kjv: she shall be put apart seven days
mine: she shall be in her menstrual impurity for seven days
note: Hebrew tihyeh beniddatah, "she shall be in her niddah (menstrual impurity)"; niddah names the state of impurity, and the text does not prescribe physical seclusion as "put apart" suggests.

mine: her menstrual impurity comes upon him
note: Hebrew niddatah, "her menstrual impurity"; "flowers" was an older English term for menstruation that modern readers will not recognise (also v. 33).
Hebrew tor is the turtledove; "turtle" in 1611 meant the bird, but now suggests the reptile.
